titleStmt.title: Digital description of MS. Canonici Or. 106

msItem.title: Pentateuch and Hafṭarot
תורה והפטרות
msItem.note: With masorah parva and magna throughout.
The haftarot for Rosh ha-Shanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkot are found at the end of the manuscript (ff. 291v-299r). The text is vocalised up to the end of f. 293r.

At the beginning of the manuscript (ff. 1v-8v) and on f. 291r, miscellaneous poems including several dedicated to individuals named Yaʿaḳov יעקוב and Avraham אברהם; one of the poems (f. 5r) mentions the death of Sinai Avraham סיני אברהם on 6 Elul 5323 (1563); another poem (f. 5v-6r) commemorates the circumscision of Gavriʾel Levi ben Shlomoh גבריאל לוי בן שלמה (date unknown). Apart from the poems, there is also a list of parashiyot to be read on festivals, fast days and special sabbaths, and their corresponding page numbers in the same manuscript, added by a later hand (f. 3r-v).

handDesc.summary: Italian-Sephardi square and Italian semi-cursive script.
handDesc.handNote: The Pentateuch (including the masorah; ff. 9-290) is in Italo-Sephardic square script; both the short haftarot section at the end (ff. 291-299) and most of the materials at the beginning (ff. 1-8) are in Italian semi-cursive script. The only exception is the list of parashiyot (f. 3r-v) which is in Italo-Sephardic square script.
The name Avraham אברהם is pointed out several times (ff. 23r, 28v, 284v); this is most likely the name of the scribe. The scribe may have been Abraham ben Mordecai Farissol.

The poems and the haftarot section were most likely copied by two different hands. The former alternated between different registers of the semi-cursive script, with some being smaller and more current, and other being larger and more calligraphic; the latter was consistently more calligraphic, with a Sephardic inflection.

decoDesc.p: On f. 8v, a very fine drawing of a menorah decorated with fleurs-de-lis. The enlarged initial words of Genesis, Exodus and Leviticus (ff. 9r, 79v, 139r) are filled with abstract penwork; those for Numbers and Deuteronomy (ff. 181r, 240r) have merely been outlined. Throughout the manuscript, some of the masorah magna along the lower margin have been written in micrography, forming simple semicircles.

bindingDesc.p: Fine-grained maroon leather (blind-tooled with a Greek key pattern) over paper boards. On the spine, two black leather labels bearing a description of the book ('LIBRI MOYSIS ETC. HEBRAICE. COD. MEM.') and the current shelfmark ('CAN. OR. 106.') respectively.
bindingDesc.condition: Some wormholes on the upper board and on the spine.

history.acquisition: Matteo Luigi Canonici's (1727-1805) collections passed to his brother Giuseppe, and on his death in 1807 to Giovanni Perissinotti and Girolamo Cardina, who divided them. To the former fell the MSS., then about 3550 in number, and, after many attempts to sell them, the Bodleian became the purchaser of the greater part in 1817, for £5444 5s. 1d., or including incidental expenses about £6030, the largest single purchase ever made by the Library. The formal list of volumes handed over was signed on May 18, 1817, and the books probably arrived later that year.
